facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness
A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness

concepts.why: The patient presented with epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, a history of amenorrhea, and a β-hCG level of 523 IU/L, which are consistent with an ectopic pregnancy.
The patient has a 1.2 cm left adnexal structure with minimal vascularity posterior to the left ovary, which could be an ovarian cyst or torsion.
The patient presented with epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen and tenderness without rebound or guarding, which could be consistent with appendicitis.
The patient has a high white blood cell count and epigastric tenderness, which could be consistent with pelvic inflammatory disease.
The patient presented with epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, which could be consistent with a gastrointestinal disorder.
The patient has a small amount of free fluid in the pouch of Douglas, which could be consistent with a ruptured ovarian cyst.
The patient has a 1.2 cm left adnexal structure with minimal vascularity posterior to the left ovary, which could be consistent with torsion of the ovary.
The patient has a β-hCG level of 523 IU/L, which could be consistent with an intrauterine pregnancy, although the ultrasound showed an empty uterus.

rationales.F04: Short duration of amenorrhea increases the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F05: Epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen is a common symptom of ectopic pregnancy and other gynecological conditions.
rationales.F09: Negative Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs decrease the likelihood of appendicitis.
rationales.F11: β-hCG level of 523 IU/L is below the discriminatory zone, increasing the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F12: Empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness on ultrasound is highly suggestive of ectopic pregnancy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with amenorrhea, epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, and a β-hCG level below the discriminatory zone, combined with an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound, strongly supports the diagnosis of an ectopic pregnancy.
